questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, where should you position yourself in the lane?

options.text: Always stay away from the left side of the lane.
Always stay away from the right side of the lane.
Always stay away from the center of the lane.
Use whatever part of the lane is safest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whatever part of the lane is safest.
questions.explanation: There is no lane position you must always avoid. Change your position based on road conditions.

questions.question: When should a motorcyclist shift gears?

options.text: During a turn.
Before a turn.
By changing power suddenly in a turn.
While braking throughout a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before a turn.
questions.explanation: You should shift gears before you enter a turn.

questions.question: Your body gets rid of one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drinks 7 drinks in 3 hours, how many drinks will be in their system 3 hours after their last drink?

options.text: Two
Three
Four
Five

questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours since the last drink from the total drinks consumed. A person who drank 7 drinks in 3 hours would have about 4 drinks left in their system 3 hours later.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever on a motorcycle?

options.text: On the left handlebar
On the right handlebar
Near the left foot peg
Near the right foot peg

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handlebar
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handlebar. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are tired while riding.
When you slow down where drivers won't expect it.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your turn signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you slow down where drivers won't expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are hard to see. Flash your brake light before slowing down in unexpected places, like the middle of a block or near an alley.

questions.question: What is the best sitting position for riding?

options.text: One where your arms hold you up.
One where you can easily reach the controls.
One where your arms are straight when holding the grips.
One where your knees stay away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: One where you can easily reach the controls.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms for steering, not for holding yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.

questions.question: Where do motorcycle operators face the most conflict with other drivers?

options.text: At intersections
On highways
On rural roads
In parking lots

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcyclists and other drivers. Be extra careful at intersections.

questions.question: If you are riding in a vehicle's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Stay where you are to avoid surprising the driver.
Wave at the driver to get their attention.
Slow down to get out of the blind spot.
Pull over to the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to get out of the blind spot.
questions.explanation: If you are in a blind spot, speed up or slow down to leave it.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle passenger never do?

options.text: Wear a helmet.
Lean when the operator leans.
Wear tight clothing.
Ride sidesaddle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride sidesaddle.
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. All riders should wear helmets. Passengers should avoid loose clothing that might catch and should lean with the operator during turns. Never let a passenger ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: What makes riding at night safer?

options.text: It is not safe and should be avoided.
Wearing reflective clothing.
Other drivers can see your turn signals better.
Only riding in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials when riding at night so other drivers can see you.

questions.question: When you slow down or stop, what should you do?

options.text: Shift up through the gears.
Shift down through the gears.
Take the bike out of gear.
Stay in the same gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. End in first gear so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What lane position is best?

options.text: It gives less space cushion but lets others see you.
It gives more space cushion and lets others see you.
It increases road hazards but lets others pass you.
It reduces road hazards but lets you follow closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives more space cushion and lets others see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position gives you more space around you and makes you visible to other drivers. It helps you avoid wind, blind spots, and hazards. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: Why use both front and rear brakes when slowing or stopping?

options.text: Using one brake causes uneven wear.
It builds good habits for emergencies.
It is the only way to slow a motorcycle.
The brakes only work when both are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: It builds good habits for emergencies.
questions.explanation: Using both brakes in normal stops helps you build the habit of always using both. This habit is critical in emergencies.

questions.question: What are the penalties for drinking and riding?

options.text: Severe.
Up to a judge to decide.
Not too harsh.
Optional.

questions.correctAnswerText: Severe.
questions.explanation: Oregon law has severe mandatory penalties for drinking and riding. It is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What happens if you shift into a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: The motorcycle will jerk and the rear tire may skid.
The motorcycle will speed up too quickly.
The front tire will skid.
The engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle will jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, the motorcycle will jerk and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax on the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the handgrips firmly, ease off the throttle, and stay straight. Gradually brake only on the good tire. Slowly move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, what should they do?

options.text: Lean as you lean.
Hold onto the motorcycle seat.
Sit as far back as possible.
Never hold onto you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean as you lean.
questions.explanation: A passenger should lean with you through turns and curves. They should sit as far forward as possible without interfering with your control. They should hold onto passenger handholds, or your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Downshift.
Speed up.
Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Gradually apply your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up because this makes wobbling worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle. Move your weight forward and down, and pull to the side of the road. Do not brake, as this may also worsen the wobble.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, what should you do?

options.text: Ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Assume the driver sees you.
Ride on the far left side of the lane.
Ride on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Riding in the center of the lane usually puts you in the middle of their mirror, where they are most likely to notice you.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake control usually located?

options.text: On the right handlebar.
On the left handlebar.
Near the left foot.
Near the right foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot.
questions.explanation: The rear brake on a motorcycle is operated with your right foot.

questions.question: What does it mean when a driver makes eye contact with you?

options.text: It means they see you.
It will never happen.
It does not mean they will yield to you.
It guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume a driver will yield just because they look at you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but fail to notice them.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not necessary if you have a windshield.
It only protects your eyes.
It helps protect your whole face.
It does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: How should you brake?

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam on the front brake and grab the rear brake.
Press the front brake and jam on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: To brake correctly, squeeze the front brake lever and press down on the rear brake pedal. Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.question: What should you do to help drivers merge onto the highway from an entrance ramp?

options.text: Stay in your lane.
Move to another lane if possible.
Do not worry about it since they are merging.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane if possible.
questions.explanation: Drivers merging onto the highway may not see your motorcycle. Give them space to merge safely by changing lanes if you can.
